content.user_title: Build Azure Service Bus Apps in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure Service Bus applications need correct queue, topic, session, and settlement patterns. This skill provides TypeScript SDK guidance for sending, receiving, scheduling, deferring, and dead-lettering messages.
actual_capabilities: Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential authentication with a Service Bus namespace.
Provides queue sender and receiver examples for single and batched messages.
Covers topics, subscriptions, sessions, scheduled messages, and deferred messages.
Explains dead-letter queue handling and receive modes.
Lists key SDK types for TypeScript implementations.
limitations: Does not create Azure Service Bus resources or infrastructure templates.
Does not manage secrets, connection strings, or Azure role assignments.
Does not include full production monitoring or deployment guidance.
Assumes use of the Azure Service Bus JavaScript SDK in TypeScript projects.

use_cases.title: Create Queue-Based Workflows
use_cases.description: Implement message producers and consumers with send, receive, batch, and settlement patterns.

use_cases.title: Design Publish-Subscribe Messaging
use_cases.description: Plan topic and subscription flows for event-driven application components.

use_cases.title: Improve Message Reliability
use_cases.description: Add dead-letter handling, message deferral, scheduled delivery, and session-based ordering.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Sender
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a TypeScript Azure Service Bus queue sender using DefaultAzureCredential and a named queue.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Queue Receiver
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a TypeScript receiver that reads a small batch, processes each message, and completes messages safely.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Topics and Subscriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map a TypeScript topic sender and subscription receiver for order events with application properties.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reliable Session Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a session-based workflow with ordered messages, session state, dead-letter handling, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Create a queue sender for order messages.
output_examples.output: A TypeScript implementation plan covering package setup, credential selection, sender creation, message body shape, batching, and resource cleanup.

output_examples.input: Explain how to handle failed messages.
output_examples.output: A reliability checklist covering validation failures, dead-letter reasons, dead-letter queue processing, and when to complete or reprocess messages.

output_examples.input: Design an ordered workflow with Service Bus sessions.
output_examples.output: A session design covering session identifiers, accepting a session receiver, reading session state, updating progress, and closing resources.

best_practices: Use Entra ID authentication for production workloads when possible.
Create ServiceBusClient once and reuse it across senders and receivers.
Close senders and receivers, handle process errors, and monitor dead-letter queues.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on production connection strings when managed identity or Entra ID is available.
Do not use receive-and-delete mode for messages that require reliable processing.
Do not ignore processError callbacks or dead-letter queue messages.

faq.question: Does this skill support both queues and topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for queue senders and receivers, plus topic senders and subscription receivers.

faq.question: Does it use Azure identity authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The authentication example uses DefaultAzureCredential with a fully qualified Service Bus namespace.

faq.question: Can it help with ordered message processing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Service Bus sessions, session receivers, and session state for ordered workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover dead-letter queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to dead-letter a message and process messages from the dead-letter subqueue.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on TypeScript SDK usage after the Service Bus namespace and entities already exist.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
